correctness.rationale: Permuting worlds within a signature class fixes the valuation and preserves the order, hence all term values are unions of classes. For a nonempty generator contained in U, adjoining its pseudocomplement gives U. For a proper generator meeting L, intersecting it with the upward closure of its complement gives U. Relative complements are then given by restricting pseudocomplement to the bottom Boolean interval, and adjoining U to co-negation in the top interval. Thus both Boolean intervals realize every signature-class union and share just U; the all-constant tuple instead generates only the extrema. Injectivity forces the two ceiling-log budgets and is achieved at that budget by including a lower all-ones signature (except that the two-singleton chain needs U itself as a generator). Choosing the upper coordinates and then distinct labeled words gives the falling factorial; inclusion–exclusion removes all-zero lower coordinate columns, which would be assigned to the wrong type. The subtraction of the constant 2^k tuples is needed only for two singleton levels and handles k=0. In the balanced random model, conditioning on the coordinate-type set gives independent uniform upper words and lower bits conditioned on nonzero columns; the error from dropping that condition is at most k_t 2^−t. Birthday bounds make either injectivity factor essentially a step at 2 log₂t outside a strip of diverging width o(√log₂t); binomial anti-concentration handles the strips. The type count has mean k_t/2+o(1), variance asymptotic to log₂t, and a normal limit under this scaling. Both sides clear the birthday boundary on the limiting centered interval (−c/2,c/2) for c>0; at c=0 the mass vanishes by continuity, and c<0 cannot give a nonempty interval. This yields the claimed Gaussian formula.
correctness.verification: Independent bit-mask semantic enumeration over 1≤m,n≤3 and 0≤k≤3 closed each ordered tuple under intersection, union and both residuals using down/up closures and compared size and full-generator counts. It matched 8,936 tuples and 36 census cases, including counts 0,1,5 at k=0,1,2 for m=n=1. The frozen CHECKER.py and VERIFICATION.md provide the separate recorded replay, python3 CHECKER.py in the record directory, with the same finite range; the uploaded code was not executed in the review. Neither test establishes the Gaussian limit.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A one-budget birthday estimate is a component of the proof, but does not imply the two-budget normal-window limit. The additional junction and relative-complement argument is needed to connect injectivity to exact generation and enumerate the coordinate types.

evidence: Proposition 18 identifies definability with double-Heyting generation for general bi-intuitionistic models. Resultary fa9265d0f358 describes a closely analogous complete two-level generation problem using Heyting operations, not both residuals; its main file was not available.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Definability and algebra generation are already equivalent, but forgetting co-implication does change generation. For two lower worlds and one upper world, a generator comprising U and one lower world generates the full double-Heyting algebra; with Heyting operations alone it generates only the constants and itself. This rules out identifying the two generation problems without additional argument.

value.rationale: These are natural generation invariants of an explicit finite frame family: the signature description identifies the actual definable sets and supplies an exact count for each alphabet size. It also explains why typical uniform generation needs roughly twice the optimum deterministic budget and why the random window is Gaussian rather than a single fixed-budget birthday transition. This gives a useful complete calculation on a nontrivial family without claiming general height-two or nonuniform results.
